title: Implement fractional and whole share order sizing under stop-based loss budget
description:
Implement pure, deterministic long-entry position sizing in mike_trade/portfolio/sizing.py. Inputs (all Decimal, no floats): reference/limit entry price, remaining symbol budget, remaining total budget, broker buying power, configured reserve and slippage cushion, allowed share precision (whole shares or provider-supported fractional increment), minimum order value, optional or required max_planned_loss_usd, validated protective stop price/distance, and a provider capability descriptor indicating whether fractional quantities and the selected protection type (fixed stop, broker-native trailing stop, stepped trailing) are supported together. Algorithm: compute the spendable notional as min(remaining symbol budget, remaining total budget, broker buying power minus reserve) adjusted down by the slippage cushion; if max_planned_loss_usd is configured, also cap quantity at max_planned_loss_usd / (entry price - stop price) and require a validated stop strictly below entry for longs (reject if missing when required, zero, or non-positive distance); round DOWN (ROUND_DOWN) to the allowed precision; return a sizing result with quantity, notional, planned loss, and an explicit rejection reason enum when it cannot size. Must reject: quantity rounds to zero or below minimum order value; insufficient buying power; fractional quantity requested but provider/protection combination unsupported (fail closed: fractional+trailing combos remain unavailable unless capability explicitly marked demonstrated); protection cannot be established; margin use when margin not explicitly enabled. Short sizing is not enabled: requesting a short side must be rejected. Write positive and negative unit tests in tests/unit/test_position_sizing.py.

Before editing, inspect:
- Existing Decimal money/quantity domain types and rounding helpers (mike_trade/domain/ or equivalent)
- Existing broker/provider capability descriptors for fractional and trailing-stop support (mike_trade/brokers/ or ports created in earlier phases)
- Existing protective-stop validation types (mike_trade/protection/ or equivalent)
- Existing configuration models for reserve, slippage cushion, min order value, max_planned_loss_usd

Decision budget: keep sizing a pure function/class with no I/O, no broker calls, and no persistence; do not edit capability or config modules — accept them as inputs or define minimal Protocols in sizing.py.
acceptance_criteria: mike_trade/portfolio/sizing.py exposes a pure sizing function or class that performs no I/O and uses only Decimal arithmetic with ROUND_DOWN to the allowed precision
A test proves quantity is bounded by the minimum of remaining symbol budget, remaining total budget, and broker buying power minus reserve and slippage cushion
A test proves that with max_planned_loss_usd configured, quantity * (entry - stop) never exceeds max_planned_loss_usd
A test proves a missing, equal-to-entry, or above-entry stop is rejected when max_planned_loss_usd is required
A test proves whole-share precision rounds down (e.g. computed 7.9 shares yields 7) and a result of 0 is rejected with an explicit reason
A test proves a quantity whose notional is below minimum order value is rejected

A test proves a fractional quantity is rejected (fail closed) when the provider capability does not support fractional with the selected protection type, and accepted when the capability is explicitly marked supported
A test proves insufficient broker buying power and margin-not-enabled cases are rejected with distinct reason codes
A test proves a short-side sizing request is rejected
tests/unit/test_position_sizing.py passes when run on its own with pytest
forbidden_changes: change PLAN_SKELETON.json or other planning artifacts
use float for money or quantities
perform broker, network, or database I/O in sizing
run broad test suites or backtests
